html:
In February and March 2002 the state of Gujarat saw the worst violence between Hindus and Muslims in India since the 1990s. More than a thousand people were killed, most of them Muslims.

On 27 February a train carrying Hindu activists home from Ayodhya stopped at Godhra (see the Babri Masjid). After a fight on the platform a coach was set on fire, and 59 people burnt to death, many of them women and children. A Muslim crowd was blamed, and 31 men were later convicted.

From the next day mobs attacked Muslim homes, shops and mosques in Ahmedabad and across the state. In one housing estate 69 people were killed, among them a former member of parliament who had phoned for help for hours. Women were raped and families burnt alive. The official count is 790 Muslims and 254 Hindus dead; others put the total near 2,000. About 150,000 people fled to camps.

The state's chief minister was Narendra Modi, five months in office. Critics charged that his government let the killing run and that police stood by. A team appointed by the Supreme Court found no grounds to prosecute him, and the court upheld that in 2022. Other cases led to convictions, some of them of politicians.
sum: In February and March 2002 the state of Gujarat saw the worst violence between Hindus and Muslims in India since the 1990s. More than a thousand people were killed, most of them Muslims.
